reconstructed_theorem_text: For every three measurable spaces A, B, and C, every probability measure mu on A, every pair of Markov probability kernels K and L from A to B, every Markov probability kernel S from B to C, and every function epsilon : A -> R integrable with respect to mu, the following implication holds. Suppose that for mu-almost every x in A, simultaneously for every measurable set s in B, |K(x,s) - L(x,s)| <= epsilon(x). Then for every measurable set t in C, |integral_A integral_B S(y,t) K(x,dy) mu(dx) - integral_A integral_B S(y,t) L(x,dy) mu(dx)| <= integral_A epsilon(x) mu(dx). The two integrals inside the absolute value are the real event masses obtained by first applying K or L to mu and then applying the same kernel S. All kernels are probability kernels, so these event masses are finite. The exceptional mu-null set is common to all measurable s. No separate pointwise nonnegativity assumption on epsilon is imposed.
objects: Measurable spaces A, B, and C; a probability measure mu on A; Markov kernels K and L from A to B; one common downstream Markov kernel S from B to C; an integrable real budget epsilon on A; the resulting two probability measures on C; measurable events s in B and t in C.
domains: A, B, and C are arbitrary measurable spaces. mu is a probability measure on A. K and L are measurable probability kernels A -> B, and S is a measurable probability kernel B -> C. epsilon : A -> R is integrable under mu. The hypothesis compares real event masses in B, and the conclusion compares real event masses in C.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over A, B, C, mu, K, L, S, and epsilon satisfying the assumptions. The hypothesis has the order: for mu-almost every x, for every measurable s in B, the discrepancy is at most epsilon(x). For each such choice of the same S on both sides, the conclusion holds for every measurable t in C.
assumptions: mu is a probability measure; K, L, and S are Markov probability kernels with the specified input and output spaces; epsilon is integrable under mu; and |K(x,s)-L(x,s)| <= epsilon(x) simultaneously for every measurable s at mu-almost every x.
conclusion: For every measurable t in C, the absolute difference between the real t-masses of (S composed with K)_*mu and (S composed with L)_*mu is at most integral_A epsilon dmu. These masses are respectively integral_A integral_B S(y,t) K(x,dy) mu(dx) and integral_A integral_B S(y,t) L(x,dy) mu(dx).
scopes: Composition first applies K or L and then S. The same S is used on both sides; the statement does not compare two different downstream kernels. A common mu-null exceptional set covers all measurable input-stage events s. epsilon depends on the initial input x, and its integral is taken under the initial mu. All event masses are finite real values because the kernels and input measure are probabilities. No separate global pointwise nonnegativity of epsilon is assumed.
constant_dependencies: The multiplicative constant is exactly 1. The bound is integral_A epsilon dmu and has no extra dependence on S, t, or the measurable spaces, and no factor 2.
